units.title: Finite-integral function entropy
units.classification: canonical measure-theoretic library node; finite-integral domain
units.statement: For a measurable space X, a measure m, and a real function g, define its real function entropy by the difference of the integral of g log g and the mean of g times the logarithm of that mean. Applications below impose integrability explicitly; this literal real formula is not an extended-real entropy.
assumptions: Objects, quantifiers, constants and all finite-integral restrictions are stated in the adjacent statement and exact Lean.
The test predicate and energy density are fixed before changing the measure; no differential operator is transported.

units.title: An energy LSI on a fixed class of finite-integral tests
units.classification: canonical measure-theoretic library node; finite-integral domain
units.statement: Fix a measurable space X, a measure m, a real energy density Γ(f)(x), a test-function predicate D(f), and C. The finite-integral energy LSI means: every D-test f for which f², f² log(f²), and Γ(f) are integrable, with Γ(f) nonnegative almost everywhere, satisfies Ent_m(f²) ≤ 2 C ∫Γ(f) dm. It asserts no integrability outside those tests.
units.formula: \operatorname{Ent}_\mu(f^2)\le 2C\int\Gamma(f)\,d\mu,\qquad f\in D\text{ in the finite-integral domain}.
assumptions: Objects, quantifiers, constants and all finite-integral restrictions are stated in the adjacent statement and exact Lean.
The test predicate and energy density are fixed before changing the measure; no differential operator is transported.

units.title: Compare entropy under a bounded change of probability law
units.classification: canonical measure-theoretic library node; finite-integral domain
units.statement: Let μ and ν be probability measures on the same measurable space. If b ≥ 0, ν ≤ b μ, and g is nonnegative μ-almost everywhere with g and g log g μ-integrable, then Ent_ν(g) ≤ b Ent_μ(g). Integrability under ν is derived, including the zero-mean case.
assumptions: Objects, quantifiers, constants and all finite-integral restrictions are stated in the adjacent statement and exact Lean.
The test predicate and energy density are fixed before changing the measure; no differential operator is transported.

steps.title: Use a nonnegative scalar cost
steps.text: For s ≥ 0 and t > 0, the logarithm inequality gives Φ_t(s) = s log(s/t)-s+t ≥ 0. The case s=0 is handled separately, so no strict positivity of the test is assumed.
steps.lean: cost_nonneg uses Real.log_le_sub_one_of_pos and a zero split.

steps.title: Separate entropy from the cost at the mean
steps.text: Linearity of the integrable terms and probability mass one give an exact identity. The cost at the target mean is nonnegative, hence every positive t is an upper bound on entropy.
steps.lean: integrable_cost, integral_cost and entropy_le_integral_cost are private providers.

steps.title: Compare the nonnegative costs under the two laws
steps.text: Measure domination transports integrability and compares the integral of the nonnegative cost. Choose t equal to the positive reference mean; its reference cost at the mean vanishes.
steps.lean: Use integral_mono_measure after Integrable.smul_measure and mono_measure.

steps.title: Discharge zero mean
steps.text: A nonnegative integrable function with zero integral vanishes almost everywhere. Absolute continuity transfers this to the target law, so both displayed real entropies equal zero.

units.title: Transfer the same energy inequality between comparable probability laws
units.classification: canonical measure-theoretic library node; finite-integral domain
units.statement: Let μ and ν be probability measures on the same measurable space, with μ ≤ a ν and ν ≤ b μ for nonnegative finite real a,b. For the same energy density Γ and fixed test class D, an energy LSI under μ with C ≥ 0 transfers to ν with constant C a b. The conclusion covers exactly the finite-integral domain in the definition; reference-law test integrability is derived from target-law integrability.
assumptions: Objects, quantifiers, constants and all finite-integral restrictions are stated in the adjacent statement and exact Lean.
The test predicate and energy density are fixed before changing the measure; no differential operator is transported.

steps.title: Keep the test class and energy fixed
steps.text: Start with any target-law finite-integral test in D. Domination μ ≤ a ν derives all three reference-law integrability conditions, and absolute continuity transports nonnegativity of the energy.

steps.title: Transfer entropy and energy in opposite directions
steps.text: Apply the compiled entropy comparison, the reference LSI, and the integral comparison of the nonnegative energy. Nonnegativity of b and C licenses multiplication of inequalities.
steps.lean: Call entropy_le_mul_of_measure_le and integral_mono_measure; the remaining rearrangement is ring arithmetic.

units.title: Exponential perturbation with the exact oscillation factor
units.classification: canonical measure-theoretic library node; finite-integral domain
units.statement: Let μ be a probability measure on any measurable space, B an almost-everywhere measurable real function, and l,u finite real bounds with l ≤ B ≤ u μ-almost everywhere. If C ≥ 0 and the finite-integral energy LSI holds under μ for fixed Γ,D with constant C, it holds for the normalized tilt dν = exp(B)/Z dμ with constant C exp(u-l). The proof derives integrability and positivity of Z, normalization, and both measure comparisons; it does not assume the perturbed LSI.
units.formula: \nu=Z^{-1}e^B\mu,\quad l\le B\le u\quad\Longrightarrow\quad C_\nu\le C_\mu e^{u-l}.
assumptions: Objects, quantifiers, constants and all finite-integral restrictions are stated in the adjacent statement and exact Lean.
The test predicate and energy density are fixed before changing the measure; no differential operator is transported.

steps.title: Construct the normalized probability law
steps.text: The upper bound B ≤ u bounds exp B by the integrable constant exp u. Measurability gives integrability, and the strictly positive exponential has positive integral, so Z is finite and positive and the normalized tilt is a probability measure.

steps.title: Prove both density comparisons
steps.text: The same Z occurs in both bounds. The upper density is exp u / Z; multiplying the tilted density by Z / exp l makes it at least one. Both comparisons follow by monotonicity of withDensity.
steps.lean: Use withDensity_mono, withDensity_const, withDensity_one and withDensity_smul'.

steps.title: Cancel the normalization constant
steps.text: Apply the general measure-comparison transfer. Its factor is the product of the two proved bounds; Z cancels exactly, leaving exp(u-l). The test class and energy density are unchanged.
steps.lean: Apply energyLogSobolev_of_measure_comparison; use Real.exp_sub and field_simp with Z ≠ 0.
